summary.headline: Rossari Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record Rs 684.9 crore (+18% YoY), but FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% from 12.7%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and absolute EBITDA, with revenue up 18% YoY to Rs 684.9 crore and EBITDA up 11% to Rs 77.3 crore, though margin slipped to 11.3% from 12%. For FY26, revenue grew 15% (volume-driven) to Rs 2,396.4 crore while EBITDA rose 8% to Rs 286 crore. March saw raw material price increases of 25-30% that compressed gross margin, and management says these are now being passed through from April. Management rephased the Rs 192 crore capex plan across Rossari, Unitop and Tristar, guided FY27 growth of at least 15% and consolidated EBITDA margin of 12-13%, and flagged plans to exit non-core consumer and institutional businesses.

financial_highlights.metric: Core B2B EBITDA margin (ex institutional and B2C)
Other income from Mumbai office sale

segments.name: HPPC (Home, Personal Care and Performance Chemicals)
segments.commentary: Grew 18% in Q4 FY26. Management says gross margins are mixed across agro, non-agro and oil and gas; pharma is a new focus area expected to carry the highest gross margin once scaled.

segments.name: Textiles
segments.commentary: Grew 20% in Q4 FY26. Specialty textile margins described as healthy; some resistance to price pass-through in textile industry. Thailand blending unit started end-March 2026.

segments.name: AHN (Animal Health and Nutrition)
segments.commentary: Grew 14% in Q4 FY26. Highest gross margin among segments per management; premix facility commissioned, with revenue ramp expected from Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Institutional and B2C (consumer)
segments.commentary: Growth muted with losses moderating in H2 FY26. Management targets breakeven or profitability in FY27 alongside divestment of lower-margin businesses; B2C working capital about 90 days.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports grew 11% YoY in FY26, with expansion into Latin America, Europe, Southeast Asia and Africa.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of at least 15%, similar to FY26, with upside if the global situation improves; includes Thailand (Rs 50-75 crore peak revenue, inside the 15%).
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 12-13% for FY27, with the same level expected in FY28; pharma and other higher-margin initiatives expected to help from H2 FY27.
FY27 capex of Rs 50-75 crore, including a pharma facility and an aroma chemicals project; the earlier Rs 192 crore plan is being rephased over FY27 and partly FY28.
Expects new Reliance EO capacity to come on stream around Q3 FY27 (December per another remark), supporting ethoxylation availability.
Targets reducing debt over the next 18 months, with a stated aim of becoming debt-free; plans to divest non-core office space and assets, timing not committed.
Expects asset turn of at least 3-4x at peak utilisation, the basis for a peak revenue potential post-capex.
capex_capacity: Total ethoxylation capacity at Dahej raised to 66,000 MTPA after Unitop commissioned additional capacity; partly capitalised in Q3 FY26 and balance in March 2026.
Ethoxylation utilisation at 90-100%, running 24/7 with no downtime outside expansion work.
Unitop 15,000 MT capacity commissioned in Q2 FY26 was about 10-15% utilised in Q3 and is ramping up in Q4 (exact figure not disclosed).
New R&D facility in Navi Mumbai consolidates existing R&D including the IIT Mumbai centre.
Premix plant for AHN commissioned; revenue expected from Q1 FY27, full-scale capacity enhancement next year.
Thailand blending unit started end-March 2026, focused on textiles with some AHN; not a full-scale plant.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is robust with no demand-side challenge; agro season depends on El Nino, with a good project pipeline.
Raw material prices rose in March (some 25-30%); management says increases have been passed through from April 1, with pass-through easy for most products and resistance in textiles.
Raw material position stable; EO is domestically sourced; phenol sourced from Thailand, Malaysia, India, China and US, and none from the Middle East now.

Competitors named: Kemin, Cargill, Novus, Zoetis (Vetnex), Natural Remedies, Jubilant (AHN); Archroma, Croda, CHT, Pulcra (textiles); BASF, Dow, Lubrizol, Syensqo, Evonik, SABIC, India Glycols (HPPC).
Top 10 customers about 12-13% of revenue; no single customer above 2% of sales. Sales grew at 25% CAGR over six years, with profit CAGR of 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What growth and consolidated EBITDA margin should shareholders expect for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided minimum growth similar to FY26 (about 15%) and EBITDA margin of 12-13%, maintained in FY27, with pharma initiatives adding from H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the capex postponed after being announced a year earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethoxylation capex was delayed as Reliance revised its expansion plans. The April 2025 plan (amines, pilot plants, R&D; about Rs 190 crore) is rephased over FY27 and partly FY28 for cash flow and ROCE reasons; the R&D spend has moved to Navi Mumbai.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a share buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans for a buyback, per Ketan Sablok.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Thailand plant's revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak revenue of Rs 50-75 crore, included within the 15% FY27 growth target; meaningful ramp-up expected from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the institutional business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects breakeven or profitability in FY27, along with divesting lower-margin businesses; FY27 should be a very good year for the institutional business.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any rumours of promoter stake sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Chari said there is nothing of such at all and no plan at this moment.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and raw material volatility could affect margins and supply chains over coming quarters.
Dependence on EO supply: utilisation is at 90-100%, and further Reliance EO capacity is expected around Q3 FY27 (December per another remark).
Margin guidance of 12-13% depends on pass-through holding in textiles and on the success of pharma and other higher-margin initiatives.
Institutional and B2C losses; breakeven is targeted for FY27 but not yet demonstrated.
Non-core asset divestment has no committed value or timeline; management said it could take one to two years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, the Q4 record and the 15% growth target, but cautious on the external environment and the margin outlook. Management was evasive on segment-level margins, divestment values and the Rs 192 crore capex specifics.
key_quotes: We concluded FY 26 on a very strong note, with Q4 marking our highest -ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA performance.
Currently, the EBITDA margins will remain at these current levels between 12% to 13%.
Utilization levels for ethoxylation are practically 90% to 100%, whatever maximum we can do.
The target is to actually get debt free in the next 18 months, but the time will tell.

Dahej ethoxylation total raised to 66,000 MTPA after Unitop additional capacity (balance capitalised March 2026)
AHN premix plant (revenue ramp from Q1 FY27; full-scale capacity enhancement next year)
Thailand blending unit (textiles, some AHN; not full-scale; Rs 50-75 crore peak revenue potential)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at least 15% (similar to FY26) and EBITDA margin 12-13%, backed partly by Unitop/Dahej ethoxylation capacity (66,000 MTPA, 90-100% utilised), AHN premix ramp from Q1 FY27 and Thailand blending unit, but the Rs 192 crore capex was cut to Rs 50-75 crore for FY27 and the Reliance EO capacity timing is unresolved.
